title: Update
objective: Users check for, preview, start, schedule, follow, hold, repair, roll back, diagnose and clean up OpenClaw updates and Gateway restarts from the terminal, the Control UI, chat, the agent and automatic campaigns, normally on an installation older than the target with a newer release published, a turn in flight, plugins and legacy state and config to migrate, and through failures, interruptions, recovery and restarts.

phases.intent: A newer OpenClaw release (the side's own build and a version-bumped copy of it) is published on the stable, beta and extended-stable channels of a local release feed the environment's update checks and package tools use, so every later phase runs with an update available; the feed's published targets are observed.

A user checks whether an update is available and what is installed, from the CLI, the Gateway method, the status summary and the Settings Updates page, with failed and stale runs on record and a release published; the reported channel, availability, install facts, recorded runs and the page are observed.

An operator brings legacy state and config forward: the first start of the side over the persona's older state is read back from logs, status and Doctor, then doctor --fix runs on it and on environments holding retired JSON state, retired config keys and a legacy agents.list roster, with a dry-run update on the retired ones; migration receipts, refusals, warnings, ready check and the repaired config are observed.
A user creates a verified backup before an update; the archive manifest and verification result are observed.

A user updates OpenClaw from a terminal with piped input while a turn is in flight: a dry run with the live config, then with an invalid field and with a missing plugin load path, then a real update of an npm global installation from the persona's older release to the published side release (reading update status mid-run and running from inside the installation directory), of the OCM-managed environment, and of an installation without a owning package tool and of a Bun-owned installation whose Gateway then starts on Bun; dry-run notes, admission, phases, warnings, verification facts, downtime, status and Doctor findings are observed.

A user re-runs the update when only the external plugin has a newer release and a plugin migration is pending, then lets Doctor finish the migration; plugin convergence warnings, the restart decision, migrationWarnings and plugin list are observed.

A user previews and switches the release channel and install type: dry runs for beta and extended-stable, the Settings channel selector, the update wizard declined at its prompt, a dev-channel update and a switch back to the stable package on a Git checkout, and dev switches refused on a dirty checkout and a pnpm-owned installation; selected targets, saved channel, plugin source sync, refusals and service recovery are observed.

An administrator reviews the available update from the sidebar card and cancels it, then starts it from Settings Updates with Update now and Update and restart while a turn is in flight, follows the phase list and step disclosures through the restart and closes the final report; the confirmation, live phases, reconnect state, report and the recorded run are observed.

An owner sends /update in the main session, then asks the agent to update so it calls the gateway tool's update.run action, a scheduled job asks for an update under its own authority, and a non-owner direct peer sends /update; acknowledgements, restart and final notices, refusals and the recorded runs are observed.

A user starts an update through update.run from the main session, waits for the Gateway to come back and reads the restart notice in the transcript, the Update restart row in status and the sidebar's Server updated refresh; the sentinel, notices, status row and UI refresh are observed.

An administrator turns automatic updates on for the stable channel, reads the announced campaign, holds it for an hour from the Settings page and the sidebar card and through update.hold, then turns update checks off and on again; the campaign state, hold deadline, toggles and logs are observed.
An operator lists recent update runs and reads one at the history limit through the Gateway and the CLI; the run records, compacted steps and status fields are observed.

An administrator checks the status of a recorded update attempt from the page and from the update dialog, then starts Retry update and cancels at the confirmation; the status banners, dialog states and the absence of a new run are observed.

A user collects triage diagnostics for a recorded failed update from the CLI with and without JSON, and opens Diagnose update, the terminal commands and the troubleshooting link on the Settings page, with no coding agent on PATH; the saved prompt, archive, handoff commands, detected agents and the page are observed.

An owner previews the sanitized failure report for a recorded failed update through update.report and from Settings Updates, cancels once, then submits with the host GitHub CLI unavailable and opens the prefilled issue link; the preview body, fallback result and links are observed.

An operator repairs an installation after an update: update repair with plugin migrations pending, a missing install record, widened plugin capabilities and a drifted pin, a lightweight repair of a stale run, Doctor inspection, the package recovery helper status, and repair with the Gateway already stopped; finalization results, reconciled runs, warnings and service state are observed.

A user replaces OpenClaw with npm and with pnpm outside the updater while the Gateway keeps running, and updates a Git server with the reference source-server script; the Gateway's replacement record and drain, status, update status and Doctor findings are observed.

A headless node host attached to the Gateway checks the published release, prepares it and activates it once idle, or defers while busy; node update preparation, deferral, activation and the reported node version are observed.

A user restarts the Gateway while a turn is in flight and a message arrives during the drain: a safe restart, the restart preflight and request methods, /restart from chat, a SIGUSR2 signal, a plain restart and a stop request followed by a service start; drain logs, rejected input, ready check, the restart history and the in-flight turn's outcome are observed.

An operator runs the Gateway under an external supervisor, negotiates restart-handoff capabilities, requests a restart, consumes the handoff and tries a self-update that the mode refuses; capabilities, handoff results, refusal and ready check are observed.

A non-interactive update of the side to a newer build of itself fails post-activation verification because the test channel's probe fails, so the failed run enters recovery triage after service recovery; the run outcome, triage diagnostics, handoff commands and service state are observed.

An update of the side to a newer build with unchanged schemas fails post-activation verification, so the updater restores and verifies the previous generation; the rolled-back outcome, exit status, absence of triage and the serving version are observed.

After a failed post-activation verification the recovery guidance reports the latest observed service state and serving version; the guidance, recorded serving facts and the Updates page are observed.

A dev-channel update of a Git checkout fails late verification because the channel probe fails, so configuration, source and runtime are restored and the verified service restarted; the restored branch and runtime, advisories and service are observed.

An update of an npm installation from the persona's release to the side migrates state and then fails verification, so rollback is refused and the non-interactive run collects diagnostics and attempts owned repair on configured inference; refusal reason, diagnostics, repair attempt and service are observed.
With rollback unsafe after a migrated update, bounded unattended repair runs before triage on the mock provider; repair attempts, their summaries and the preserved failed outcome are observed.

A failed interactive update shows the failure menu; the user chooses Report update failure with no GitHub CLI available and then the default Exit; the menu, the return to it after the failed upload, exit status and preserved report are observed.
A failed interactive update offers to launch triage and nobody answers for 30 seconds, so the launch is skipped; the consent prompt, skip, manual command and exit status are observed.
An update started from Settings Updates fails while the Gateway handles the request; the Gateway warning log, the dialog's failure state and the recorded run are observed.

A failed Control UI update opens Ask OpenClaw once for that attempt, and with browser storage blocked no automatic diagnostic request is sent; the Ask OpenClaw panel, its prompt and the stored attempt identities are observed.

A Gateway-started update whose managed child refuses before parking the service (the config carries an invalid field) leaves the serving Gateway untouched; the refusal on the requested step, the restored config and the Gateway are observed.
The detached update helper is killed during validation so the managed child produces no usable result; managed-service-handoff-failed, the history row and the serving Gateway are observed.
The update helper cannot be spawned because its private directory is not writable; the bounded failure kind, next step and the Gateway's continued serving are observed.
An npm installation's global prefix is made read-only before an update; the global-install-permission-denied refusal, sanitized npm lines, permission guidance and untouched Gateway are observed.
The npm prefix volume of an installation fills up during the update; the ENOSPC record, guidance and rollback are observed.
Temporary storage for update snapshots is too small on every destination; the measured sizes, checked destinations, snapshot-capacity refusal or disk-space warning and untouched Gateway are observed.
The checkout's artifact area runs out of space during a dev update's staging build; preflight-insufficient-space, the preserved checkout and the serving Gateway are observed.
The published target's package is withdrawn from the release feed after its tag resolves; the npm error code, stale-cache retry warning and refusal are observed.
The release feed is unreachable when an update resolves its target; the metadata failure fact, update mode, next step and untouched installation are observed.

An update to the persona's older release is refused before mutation because the side already migrated state past it; the database-schema refusal, removed stage, unchanged package and serving Gateway are observed.

An npm installation's update fails before activation because snapshot space is short, so recovery observes the existing Gateway once without restarting it; the observation, failure and service are observed.
An update that switches to beta is refused, so the saved channel stays as it was; the refusal and the saved update.channel are observed.

An npm installation's update runs with an explicit one-second per-step deadline so the aggregate activation deadline expires; update-activation-timeout, retained ownership and recovery guidance are observed.
A Git checkout switches to the stable package and activation fails verification; the restored install link, unverified recovery and stopped service are observed.
A user updates the running side with --no-restart; the refusal to replace runtime files in use, the named process and the stop-and-retry action are observed.

After an npm installation is updated with --no-restart, the running Gateway's installation-change watcher notices the replacement and restarts; the watcher's record, restart and ready check are observed.

An update stops the Gateway for activation while a turn is in flight and the step deadline is shorter than the turn; the drain progress, interrupted turn warning and write-custody handling are observed.
After the canary passes, previous-Gateway ready check verification runs out of its explicit allowance; the warning, unverified ready check and blocked automatic restart are observed.
An npm installation is replaced underneath its running Gateway, then updated; the Gateway that can no longer serve RPC is stopped through its service owner and the warning is observed.

An npm installation is replaced with the side's package while its Gateway runs, and on its maintenance tick the Gateway records the replacement, stops admitting work and hands over to its service; the replacement record, drain, status and Doctor reports are observed.

After a manual replacement where Doctor failed on the live Gateway lock, the operator runs update repair with --no-restart from the updated installation; the repair result and service state are observed.
An updater is killed during activation, the operator installs the package manually and runs update repair; the superseded-by-manual-install closure, preserved artifacts and cleared gate are observed.
An npm installation's update is interrupted with SIGINT during staging; the failed interrupted entry, held owner and unchanged Gateway are observed.
An npm installation's update is cancelled during validation before package mutation; the restored original service and its verification are observed.
An npm installation's updater receives SIGTERM during activation; forward work stops, the recovery owner restores the Gateway and the report names the phase and signal, which are observed.
An npm installation's updater is killed with SIGKILL after it stopped the Gateway; the stopped Gateway, unverified recovery and recorded run are observed.
The updater is killed while it verifies the restarted side, and the Gateway or Doctor finish the run after fresh checks; the reconciled outcome and its step are observed.

The side updates to a newer build of itself on a store of thousands of sessions and several hundred agents, so the candidate's startup is slow but progressing; milestones, renewed allowances and the outcome are observed.
The restarted Gateway is still progressing through startup migration when its startup lease ends; the still-starting warning, running process and retained backups are observed.
Ready check of the restarted Gateway is not confirmed within its allowance for the same process; the skipped `gateway-readiness-unverified` outcome and retained backups are observed.
The candidate migration rehearsal of a large npm installation exceeds an explicit short budget; the candidate-migration-rehearsal message, last output and untouched Gateway are observed.
After a manual package replacement a standalone restart meets a startup migration that keeps progressing; the still-starting exit, last phase and next step are observed.
The restarted Gateway is killed while the updater verifies it, so its process changes; the failure, recovery and report are observed.

The Gateway's port is held by another process when a restart is requested, so the service supervisor accepts the restart but ready check fails; the restart result and ready check diagnostics are observed.
Another process holds the state directory while an update reaches finalization, so Doctor cannot enter maintenance; the restored service, warning and pending Doctor and plugin work are observed.
An already-current update parks the Gateway for plugin maintenance and the maintenance step is refused; the restart after Doctor writers settle and the preserved failure are observed.

A separate CLI process keeps writing the shared database while an npm installation's update runs Doctor maintenance; refused automatic restoration, state-migrated-no-rollback and the retained snapshots are observed.
The operator edits an included config file while the update verifies a candidate that then fails; the refused automatic rollback naming the changed file and the preserved state are observed.
Another process saves the configuration while update admission reads it; the reread warning, repeated checks and retained concurrent change are observed.
The config changes while Doctor plans its migrations; the reported changed input and the rerun guidance are observed.

The agent runs openclaw update from its exec shell inside the managed Gateway service; the handoff to the detached helper, exit 75, printed follow-up commands, the shell's fate and the recorded run are observed.
A stop is requested while a Gateway-started update is staging; the wait for update work, the draining state and the stopped Gateway are observed.
With commands.restart turned off, a Gateway update and /update are attempted; restart-disabled refusals and guidance are observed.
The Git checkout's tracking remote is unreachable during a dev update and status afterwards; fetch-failed, the stale-check line in status and the untouched checkout are observed.

The release feed withholds the external plugin's version for the new core while an npm installation updates; the plugin-target-unavailable advisory, retained plugin and successful core update are observed.
The release feed's ClawHub source lacks the version-matched official runtime plugin; the npm fallback, version-skew warning and retry instruction are observed.
Update repair runs while another update's driver is live; the refusal naming run, phase, driver and liveness is observed.
Update repair runs with a one-second phase deadline; the failed result, stuckPhase, Doctor output excerpts and restored service are observed.
Another process holds the state database's write lock while an update tries to admit its run with a short step deadline; the update-ledger-busy deferral and unchanged history are observed.
An explicit dry-run update on an installation whose only active row is stale and identityless supersedes it; the superseded outcome and the new run are observed.

Automatic updates on the beta channel announce a campaign while a turn is in flight, so the campaign waits for idle, counts down and applies by its hard deadline; campaign states, countdown, drain and the applied run are observed.
An automatic campaign's apply fails because the channel probe fails after activation; the ended campaign and the failure surfaced after the Gateway returns are observed.
Update checks are turned off immediately after automatic updates are enabled, while discovery is unfinished; the cancelled discovery and absent campaign are observed.
The Gateway restarts right after update discovery begins; the cancelled discovery, awaited Git processes and clean restart are observed.
The Control UI loses its connection while an update restarts the Gateway; the dialog's Gateway restarting state, automatic reconnect and resumed run view are observed.
A Control UI tab stays open while an update replaces the bundled UI, so it reloads once for the new build; the reload, ready check check and retry action are observed.
A follow-up typed in the Control UI is accepted while the Gateway restarts and re-admitted from the browser outbox after reconnect; the outbox replay and transcript are observed.
A Git checkout's switch to the stable package fails at its candidate because the feed withholds the package; the still-runnable previous command and preserved checkout are observed.
A Git checkout's channel switch is refused because another process holds its state; the recovered previous service and unchanged channel are observed.
An npm installation is replaced with lifecycle scripts skipped, then any CLI command runs; the completed pending lifecycle or reinstall guidance is observed.
A restart with a five-second drain budget meets a turn that is still running; the aborted work, recovery marker and drain logs are observed.
An external supervisor consumes a restart handoff with the wrong expected PID; the retained handoff and machine result are observed.

An npm installation still running the persona's pinned older Gateway has its package replaced in place by an update, so the old process's first shutdown may fail loading removed files; the shutdown outcome, restart through the installation owner and the run record are observed.

The config file is made read-only while an update of the side to a newer build activates, so Doctor's config write is refused and the update fails; the recorded refusal, rollback decision, restored package and database write evidence are observed.
A session-listing reader keeps polling the databases while update cleanup applies with the Gateway stopped; the Recovery destination database changed refusal and preserved originals are observed.
Doctor is interrupted while migrating an npm installation's agent databases after a manual replacement and is then rerun; the reclaimed owner, resumed work and retained backups are observed.
Doctor receives SIGTERM during transcript archive repair batches; the settled work, restored Gateway and next recovery action are observed.
Doctor is killed while capturing pre-startup migration backups and rerun; the reused completed backup group or recaptured unfinished capture is observed.
A user updates when the installed version is already the target, so the run converges plugins and finishes skipped/already-current; the update JSON and run record are observed.
A user updates to a candidate whose canary Gateway fails ready state, so the stage is discarded while the old Gateway keeps serving; the failure facts, run record and serving status are observed.

The persona's older installed updater drives this side's candidate when its canary fails ready state, so the first hop must report the candidate's real startup failure; the older updater's JSON, failure facts and serving status in the scratch environment are observed.
A user updates to a candidate whose package install exits nonzero, so the npm error excerpt is recorded and rollback is attempted; the failure facts, rollback outcome and serving status are observed.

A user re-runs an already-current update while the plugin registry is unreachable, so plugin sync keeps the installed plugin with a plugin-target-unavailable advisory; the update JSON and warnings are observed.

A plugin release that widens capabilities arrives during an update run with --yes but without --accept-capabilities, then the user repairs with --accept-capabilities; the PLUGIN_CAPABILITY_CONSENT_REQUIRED warning, retained payload and repair result are observed.
The external plugin's pinned version is republished with different integrity, so the update aborts that plugin artifact update; the plugin integrity drift warning and plugin list are observed.
The Gateway restarts while the update-check endpoint is unreachable, so the failed check does not interrupt startup; startup logs, ready state and update.status are observed.
update.checkOnStart is set to false and the Gateway restarts, so no update check, campaign or notice runs; startup logs and update.status schedule are observed, then checks are re-enabled.

An abandoned identityless update row and a legacy 2026.9.2-era admission sit in history when the Gateway restarts and the user runs repair; status guidance, reconciliation at startup and repair's reconciled runs are observed.
A group member who may chat but is not an owner sends /update, so the request is refused with owner setup guidance and no run starts; the reply and update history are observed.
The headless node's prepared runtime fails to reconnect after activation, so its launcher falls back to the previous runtime; the node's fallback messages and reported version are observed.

A user forces a restart while a turn is held open, so remaining work is cancelled at the shutdown deadline and the session is marked for recovery; the drain report, held turn outcome and session rows are observed.
A user restarts the Gateway while an isolated cron job runs, so the drain waits for its cleanup and result write; the cron run result, drain report and cron list are observed.
A message arrives while a restart is draining, so it is rejected with a restart error rather than queued into the old process; the send result and the session after restart are observed.

phases.intent: A user applies update cleanup while the Gateway and its database readers are running, so cleanup refuses for lack of exclusive offline ownership; the refusal and retained artifacts are observed.
The Gateway process is paused for 45 seconds and resumed; freeze detection, the deferred or immediate channel restart and refreshed health are observed.
The Gateway receives the same stop signal three times within five minutes through service restarts; the supervisor hint and shutdown records are observed.

The Gateway starts with legacy config keys staged into its config, so startup leaves them unchanged, prints the Doctor hint and the headless service stops; the startup refusal and logs are observed before the staged config is restored.

The Gateway starts with retired pre-July state files staged in its state directory, so startup logs a deferred-repair warning and continues; startup diagnostics and ready state are observed before the fixture is removed.

A corrupt generation is staged as the default agent's database and the Gateway restarts, so ready state stays false with the admission reason while other agents serve; Doctor findings, ready state and status are observed.
The Gateway is killed three times within five minutes; the crash-loop breaker's suppressed channel autostart, paused recovery and its later release are observed.
The side is updated to a newer build, replaced back with the side's own build and updated again; companion-table handling, disabled features and reconciled projections on each start are observed.
An npm installation updated to the side is manually replaced with the persona's older release; the newer-schema refusal at startup, exit 78, status and Doctor reports are observed.

After verifying an update, an operator previews retained migration recovery originals while the Gateway serves, stops the Gateway and retires the eligible ones with explicit consent; eligible, protected and removed artifacts, totals and the restarted Gateway are observed.
